title: Hivemind Effect on Code Generation: Shared Bugs Across AI Coding Assistants

original_idea.title: Hivemind Effect on Code Generation: Shared Bugs Across AI Coding Assistants
original_idea.problem: If multiple AI coding assistants generate structurally similar code for the same specifications, they likely share the same security vulnerabilities and logic errors.
original_idea.direction: Give identical coding prompts to GitHub Copilot, Claude, GPT-4o, and open-source alternatives; measure semantic similarity of generated code and overlap in introduced security vulnerabilities (CWE categories).
original_idea.why_it_matters: Correlated security bugs across all major AI coding tools would represent a systemic risk to software infrastructure at scale.
original_idea.relevant_context: Artificial Hivemind methodology applies directly; code similarity and vulnerability overlap can be measured with standard static analysis tools accessible to intro-ML students.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: correlated security bugs across all major AI coding tools is a direct, high-impact safety concern for software supply chains.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Intermediate: generating code from multiple tools and running static analysis is well-suited for CS students, though coordinating multiple API accesses adds complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: code similarity and CWE overlap analysis across 4+ coding assistants on a fixed set of prompts.

novelty.reasoning: Substantial existing work documents security vulnerabilities in AI-generated code and identifies common CWE patterns across tools. Georgetown CSET explicitly notes that shared training data leads to similar vulnerability rates. However, no study explicitly applies the Artificial Hivemind semantic similarity methodology to code outputs, and the framing of correlated CWE overlap as a systemic risk measure is partially novel. The vulnerability angle is well-studied; the homogeneity framing adds some novelty.

evidence.finding: Systematic review of security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code, identifying consistent CWE patterns across multiple tools.

evidence.source: The Hidden Vulnerabilities of AI-Generated Code: A Cross-Language Security (ICCV 2025)
evidence.finding: Cross-language security analysis of AI-generated code vulnerabilities.

evidence.source: Security Weaknesses of Copilot-Generated Code in GitHub (arXiv 2310.02059)
evidence.finding: Identified 733 code snippets with security weaknesses from Copilot, spanning 43 CWE categories.
